name: Kristine Vowles
headline: A designer’s eye. A real-estate perspective.
lead: Behind every beautiful space is a person with a vision. Kristine Vowles brings decades of experience in design, real estate and property presentation to the art of understanding that vision—and making it feel like home.
short_bio: Kristine founded The Luxury Look in 2013 after a long career in luxury real estate, brokerage leadership and property development. Her experience has shaped an approach that blends considered design with a practical understanding of how spaces are lived in, experienced and presented.
career_bio: Before founding The Luxury Look in 2013, Kristine held real-estate and business leadership roles with organizations including Prudential Real Estate, Westar Development, Coldwell Banker and Keller Williams. Working with agents, homeowners, buyers and development teams gave her a deep understanding of the people and priorities behind each property. That background still informs her decisions, whether the brief is a personal residence, a major renovation or a home preparing for market.
approach_bio: Kristine believes successful interiors start with listening. She considers how a room needs to function, how people should feel when they enter it, and what will make the space distinctly their own. Her work brings together architecture, layout, furnishings, texture, art and finishing details with an eye for both beauty and practicality. She welcomes collaboration with homeowners, architects, builders and fellow design professionals, turning a client’s ideas into a deliberate, cohesive direction.
beyond_bio: Beyond individual design projects, Kristine shares her experience through education, business workshops and conversations with design and real-estate professionals. The studio’s Buying Trips and sourcing experiences build on that same curiosity: discovering materials and pieces with a trained eye, then choosing what truly belongs. Whether she is discussing luxury staging in Sedona or exploring new collections, her focus remains on helping people see what a space can become.

principles.title: Listen before designing
principles.description: A home should reflect its owners, not a template. The process begins with a thoughtful conversation.

principles.title: Understand the whole property
principles.description: Design decisions are informed by how a home lives, functions and presents itself over time.

principles.title: Make every detail intentional
principles.description: Materials, proportion, furnishings and art should feel connected—never assembled by accident.
